description:
We're SolForge Explorers, a team of technology enthusiasts building Mars Mission Academy, an interactive space mission simulator for children ages 7–12.

Our goal is to combine software development, educational gaming, and real NASA datasets to teach space exploration through meaningful decisions.

Our technical focus includes Python, React, TypeScript, simulation systems, and data visualisation.

We welcome developers, designers, educators, and space enthusiasts!
summary:
**MissionVerse** is an educational space mission training project developed by Team SolForge Explorers for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

Our project focuses on helping young students understand the challenges astronauts face when living and working on Mars. It introduces important topics such as oxygen supply, energy management, food production, radiation protection, and planning for unexpected situations.

The idea behind MissionVerse is to make space science easier to understand through an interactive mission-training experience. Rather than only reading about space exploration, students can explore how different decisions may affect the safety and success of a mission.

Our goal is to combine technology, creativity, and NASA's scientific resources to encourage curiosity, critical thinking, and problem-solving among young learners.

MissionVerse is a step toward making complex space science concepts more accessible, practical, and engaging for the next generation of explorers.
details:
About MissionVerse

MissionVerse is a web-based educational project created by Team SolForge Explorers for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the challenge "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer."

The project aims to help students aged 7–12 learn about the challenges of operating a human outpost on Mars.

The Problem

Space exploration involves important engineering decisions. Astronauts must manage limited resources, maintain safe living conditions, and prepare for unexpected situations.

However, these topics can be difficult for young students to understand through traditional lessons.

MissionVerse aims to make these concepts easier to explore through a simple, interactive learning experience.

Our Solution

MissionVerse introduces students to the responsibilities of managing a space mission.

The learning experience focuses on five key areas:

  • Life Support: Understanding why astronauts need a reliable oxygen and water supply.
  • Power Management: Learning how limited energy affects mission operations.
  • Food Production: Exploring the importance of maintaining food supplies during long missions.
  • Radiation Protection: Understanding the risks of space radiation and the need for protection.
  • Mission Planning: Learning why every decision matters when resources are limited.

The project is designed to encourage students to think about the consequences of mission decisions instead of simply memorizing scientific facts.

Technology and Development

MissionVerse is delivered as a browser-accessible web application and is deployed using Vercel.

The project uses a digital learning approach that allows students to explore space-related concepts without requiring special hardware.

NASA's scientific publications and data resources provide a basis for understanding Mars, astronaut safety, and mission operations.

Creativity and Educational Value

Our approach focuses on connecting science with practical decision-making.

Rather than presenting space exploration only as reading material, MissionVerse is intended to help students understand the relationship between engineering systems and the challenges astronauts face.

Intended Impact

MissionVerse aims to:

  • Make space science more accessible to young learners.
  • Build curiosity about science, technology, engineering, and mathematics.
  • Encourage critical thinking and problem-solving.
  • Help students understand the importance of balancing resources.
  • Inspire interest in future careers in science and space exploration.

Future Improvements

Future development may include additional mission scenarios, improved educational feedback, more NASA scientific resources, and more detailed mission simulations.

Our long-term goal is to make MissionVerse a useful learning platform for students, educators, and young space enthusiasts.
